models.description:
Customer accounts for the e-commerce platform.

Represents registered buyers who can browse products, manage their wishlist and cart, place orders, write reviews, and manage their profile and addresses. Customers require authentication to access any platform features.

**Account Management:**
- Registration requires unique email and password
- Profile contains optional display name and phone number
- Supports soft deletion where orders and reviews are preserved for legal compliance
- When deleted, reviews display as "deleted user"

**Related Entities:**
- {@link shopping_mall_customer_sessions} - Authentication sessions
- {@link shopping_mall_customer_password_resets} - Password recovery tokens

**Data Preservation:**
When a customer deletes their account:
- Profile information (display_name, phone_number) is deleted
- Orders are preserved for seller records
- Reviews are preserved and shown as "deleted user"
models.name: shopping_mall_customers

plainFields.description: Customer's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all customer accounts.
plainFields.name: email

plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Stored using bcrypt or similar strong encryption algorithm.
plainFields.name: password_hash

plainFields.description: Customer's display name shown in reviews and order communications. Optional profile information that is deleted when account is soft-deleted.
plainFields.name: display_name

plainFields.description: Customer's phone number for delivery contacts and notifications. Optional profile information that is deleted when account is soft-deleted.
plainFields.name: phone_number

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was created.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was last updated.
plainFields.name: updated_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was soft-deleted. When set, the account is considered deleted but orders and reviews are preserved for legal compliance. Null means the account is active.
plainFields.name: deleted_at

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_sessions
models.description: JWT session tokens for customer authentication supporting multi-device login with device tracking. Each session stores access and refresh tokens with expiration timestamps, connection metadata (IP, href, referrer), and user agent for device identification. Sessions are created on login and invalidated on logout or token expiration. Enables secure token refresh, multi-device session management, and session revocation capabilities.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who owns this session. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token for API authentication. Short-lived token (30-minute expiration) used for authenticating API requests.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens. Long-lived token (14-day expiration) used to rotate access tokens without requiring re-login.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the customer logged in. Used for security auditing and suspicious activity detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL or page where the login was initiated. Captures the application context at login time.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header from the login request. Used for tracking login source and security analysis.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser user agent string for device identification. Enables multi-device session management and device recognition for security purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created (login time). Used for session listing and audit trail.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the refresh token. Session becomes invalid after this time and requires re-authentication.

models.description: Password reset tokens for customer email-based password recovery. Contains unique token (hashed), expiration timestamp (typically 1 hour), and usage tracking. Automatically invalidated after use or expiration. When a customer successfully resets their password, all existing sessions are invalidated for security.

foreignFields.description: The customer who requested password reset. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_password_resets

plainFields.description: Unique password reset token (hashed) sent to customer's registered email address. Used to verify identity and authorize password change. Must be unique across all reset requests.
plainFields.name: token

plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the reset token. Tokens typically expire after 1 hour for security. Expired tokens cannot be used for password reset.
plainFields.name: expires_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token was used. Null if not yet used. Used to prevent token reuse and track successful password resets.
plainFields.name: used_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset request was created. Used for audit trail and cleanup of old tokens.
plainFields.name: created_at

models.name: shopping_mall_sellers
models.description:
Registered seller accounts with email/password credentials for authentication, shop profile information, and approval status management.

Sellers operate as merchants on the platform after administrator approval. Each seller maintains a shop profile (name, description, logo) visible to customers. The approval workflow transitions seller accounts through pending → approved/rejected/suspended states.

Account deletion is conditional: sellers cannot delete their account while pending orders or cancellation/refund requests exist. Upon deletion, products and inventory are removed while order history preserves the shop name for legal compliance.

Related sessions are tracked in {@link shopping_mall_seller_sessions} and password resets in {@link shopping_mall_seller_password_resets}.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for seller login and authentication. Must be unique across all seller accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt-hashed password for secure authentication. Stored as hashed value, never in plain text.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: Display name of the seller's shop visible to customers in product listings and seller profile. Also preserved in order history after account deletion.

plainFields.name: shop_description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description of the seller's shop, business, or products. Displayed on seller profile page.

plainFields.name: logo_url
plainFields.description: URL to the seller's shop logo image. Used in seller profile and product listings for brand visibility.

plainFields.name: approval_status
plainFields.description: Current approval status of the seller account. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting admin review), 'approved' (active seller), 'rejected' (denied by admin), 'suspended' (temporarily blocked by admin).

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by administrator when rejecting a seller registration. Only populated when approval_status is 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was created (registration submitted).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was soft-deleted. Null for active accounts. Used for account deletion which is conditional on having no pending orders or requests.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_sessions

Each session record contains access and refresh tokens, device information, and connection metadata (IP, href, referrer). Sessions are created upon successful seller login and expire based on token lifecycle. Supports concurrent sessions across multiple devices with individual session management.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token for seller authentication. Short-lived token (15-30 minutes expiration) used for API requests.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens. Long-lived token (7-30 days expiration) used to refresh authentication without re-login.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the seller logged in. Used for security auditing and session tracking.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL path of the page from which login was initiated. Used for security tracking and session context.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header value from the login request. Used for security auditing and session origin tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created (seller logged in).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Based on refresh token expiration time. Session is invalid after this time.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_password_resets
models.description: Password reset tokens for seller accounts enabling email-based password recovery. Each record contains a hashed reset token linked to a specific seller, with creation and expiration timestamps for security validation. Tokens are automatically invalidated after expiration (typically 15-30 minutes) and can be used only once for password reset verification. Supports the seller authentication workflow as a subsidiary entity to the {@link shopping_mall_sellers} actor table.

foreignFields.name: seller_id

plainFields.name: token

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset request was created. Used for audit trail and rate limiting purposes.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the reset token. Tokens become invalid after this time for security purposes. Typically set to 15-30 minutes after creation.

models.description:
Administrator accounts with email/password credentials and grade level (regular/super) for elevated platform management permissions.

Administrators oversee platform operations including seller approvals, category management, product oversight, order management, and user moderation. Super administrators have additional capabilities to manage other administrator accounts and cannot demote themselves.

Related entities:
- {@link shopping_mall_admin_sessions} - Active login sessions for this administrator
- {@link shopping_mall_admin_password_resets} - Password recovery tokens
- {@link shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs} - Administrative action audit trail

models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrator email-based password recovery.

When an administrator requests a password reset, the system generates a unique reset code
and stores it in this table with an expiration time. The administrator receives the code
via email and can use it to reset their password within the validity period.

Each reset token is linked to a specific administrator account and becomes invalid after
expiration or after being used. Multiple reset tokens can exist for the same administrator
(e.g., if they request multiple resets), but typically only the most recent one is valid.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id

plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token expires. After this time, the token is no longer valid for password reset.
plainFields.name: expired_at

models.description:
Audit trail records of all administrative actions performed on the platform for security compliance, accountability, and dispute resolution.

Each record captures which administrator performed what action, on which target entity, at what time, from which IP address. Supports investigation of administrative actions including seller approvals, product removals, user bans, force-cancellations, and configuration changes.

References the administrator who performed the action via {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}. This table is append-only - records are never modified or deleted to maintain complete audit history.

foreignFields.description: The administrator who performed this action. References {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs

plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed. Examples: 'seller_approve', 'seller_reject', 'seller_suspend', 'product_delete', 'order_force_cancel', 'order_force_refund', 'customer_ban', 'customer_unban', 'category_create', 'category_update', 'category_delete', 'admin_promote', 'admin_demote'.
plainFields.name: action

plainFields.description: Category of the entity that was acted upon. Examples: 'seller', 'customer', 'product', 'order', 'category', 'admin'. Used in conjunction with target_id to identify the affected entity.
plainFields.name: target_type

plainFields.description: UUID of the specific entity that was acted upon. References the ID of the entity identified by target_type. Can be null for actions that don't target a specific entity (e.g., system configuration changes).
plainFields.name: target_id

plainFields.description: Additional contextual details about the action in JSON format. Stores action-specific information such as rejection reasons, ban durations, refund amounts, or other relevant metadata that varies by action type.
plainFields.name: details

plainFields.description: IP address from which the administrative action was performed. Used for security auditing and detecting suspicious activity patterns.
plainFields.name: ip

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrative action was performed.
plainFields.name: created_at

models.name: shopping_mall_categories
models.description: Product categories organized in a two-level hierarchy managed by administrators. Parent categories have null parent_id while subcategories reference their parent category via parent_id. Each category contains a unique name (unique among siblings within the same parent) and an optional description. Categories classify products for browsing and search functionality. When deleted, products become uncategorized rather than cascade deleted. The two-level hierarchy limit (category and subcategory only) is enforced at the application layer.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to parent category for subcategory hierarchy. Null for top-level categories. Enables two-level category structure where subcategories reference their parent category.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name, unique among siblings within the same parent category. Used for display and identification in product listings and navigation.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description of the category purpose and scope. Helps administrators and users understand category contents.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was created by an administrator.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was soft-deleted. Null for active categories. Soft deletion preserves product references while removing category from active listings.

models.description:
Main product listings created by sellers, containing name, description, category reference, base price, and soft-delete support.

Products are the primary sellable entities in the marketplace. Each product belongs to exactly one seller and can optionally be assigned to a category. Products support soft deletion to preserve order history references and enable potential recovery.

Products require at least one variant with stock to be purchasable. When a product is deleted, all variants and images are removed, but snapshots are preserved for audit purposes.

Key relationships:
- {@link shopping_mall_sellers} - Seller who owns this product
- {@link shopping_mall_categories} - Optional category assignment
- {@link shopping_mall_product_variants} - SKU variants with pricing and stock
- {@link shopping_mall_product_images} - Product images with ordering
- {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots} - Immutable state history

foreignFields.description: Seller who owns this product. Every product must have exactly one seller. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}
foreignFields.name: seller_id

foreignFields.description: Category this product belongs to. Can be null if product is uncategorized. Products become uncategorized when their category is deleted. {@link shopping_mall_categories.id}
foreignFields.name: category_id

models.name: shopping_mall_products

plainFields.description: Product name displayed in listings and search results. Required field that must be unique within the seller's products.
plainFields.name: name

plainFields.description: Detailed product description explaining features, specifications, and usage. Supports rich text formatting.
plainFields.name: description

plainFields.description: Base price for the product in the platform's currency. Individual variants can override this price. Must be a positive value.
plainFields.name: base_price

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was created. Automatically set on creation.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was last updated. Automatically updated on any modification.
plainFields.name: updated_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was soft-deleted. Null if product is active. Preserves order history references when product is removed.
plainFields.name: deleted_at

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variants
models.description: Product variants/SKUs representing specific purchasable combinations of a product. Each variant has a unique SKU code, optional price override from the product's base price, and is linked to a parent product. Variant options (such as color, size) are stored as normalized key-value pairs in the child table shopping_mall_product_variant_options. Stock quantity is tracked through inventory history records, not stored directly. Variants cannot be deleted if pending orders or cancellation/refund requests exist.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product that this variant belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: Unique SKU code identifying this variant. Must be unique across all products in the system.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Price override for this variant. If null, uses the parent product's base price. Allows different pricing for different variant combinations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft delete. When set, variant is considered deleted but preserved for order history and audit purposes. Cannot be deleted if pending orders or requests exist.

models.description:
Product images attached to products with ordering support for display sequence management.

Each product can have multiple images, and the image with the lowest order value (typically order=1) serves as the main/thumbnail image displayed in product listings and search results. Images are managed through their parent {@link shopping_mall_products} entity and are deleted when the parent product is deleted.

When product images change (add, delete, reorder), the changes are captured in {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots} for audit trail purposes per the snapshot principle. Images support seller product management workflows including upload, reordering, and deletion operations.

foreignFields.description: Product to which this image belongs. References {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id

models.name: shopping_mall_product_images

plainFields.description: URL path to the image file. Stored as a URI pointing to the image location in the storage system (e.g., CDN or object storage).
plainFields.name: url

plainFields.description: Display order of the image within the product's image gallery. Lower values appear first. The image with the lowest order value serves as the main/thumbnail image for product listings and search results. Enables drag-and-drop reordering functionality for sellers.
plainFields.name: order

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image was uploaded and attached to the product.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image metadata (e.g., order) was last modified. Updated when seller reorders images.
plainFields.name: updated_at

models.description:
Immutable product snapshots preserving complete product state at the point-in-time of any product modification.

This table implements the snapshot principle for products, ensuring complete audit trails for all product modifications. Each snapshot captures the denormalized product fields including name, description, base price, category reference, and seller reference at the moment of creation or update.

The snapshot principle requires that:
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Each snapshot records the complete state at a point in time
- Snapshots enable dispute resolution and historical tracking
- Even when products are deleted, snapshots are preserved

Variant states at snapshot time are captured separately in {@link shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots} and can be correlated via shopping_mall_product_id and created_at timestamp.

Image states at snapshot time are captured separately in {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshot_images} to maintain normalized structure while preserving the complete product state including images.

foreignFields.description: Reference to the product being snapshotted. Points to {@link shopping_mall_products.id}. Multiple snapshots exist for each product over its lifecycle, creating a complete modification history.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id

foreignFields.description: Seller who owned the product at snapshot time. Points to {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}. Enables efficient querying of a seller's product modification history and preserves seller association even if product is deleted.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id

foreignFields.description: Category the product belonged to at snapshot time. Points to {@link shopping_mall_categories.id}. Preserves category assignment for historical accuracy and audit purposes, enabling analysis of product categorization over time.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_category_id

models.name: shopping_mall_product_snapshots

plainFields.description: Product name at the time of snapshot. Stored denormalized to preserve exact wording even if product is later modified or deleted. Used for audit trails and dispute resolution.
plainFields.name: name

plainFields.description: Product description at the time of snapshot. Stored denormalized to preserve exact content including formatting and details at that point in time.
plainFields.name: description

plainFields.description: Base price of the product at snapshot time in the platform's currency. Stored denormalized to track pricing history and enable price change analysis. Actual selling price may vary by variant.
plainFields.name: base_price

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, marking the point-in-time of the product modification. Used for chronological ordering and time-based queries. Immutable once created.
plainFields.name: created_at

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots preserving the complete state of product variants at the point-in-time of product modification. Each snapshot captures the SKU code and price override of a variant, enabling complete audit trails for dispute resolution and version control.

Created automatically when a product is modified, these snapshots are linked to a parent product snapshot via {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots.id}. The combination of product snapshot and variant is unique, ensuring each variant's state is captured exactly once per product modification event.

Option values are stored in a normalized child table {@link shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshot_option_values} for proper atomicity and queryability. Each option (e.g., color, size) is stored as a separate key-value pair.

These snapshots serve as the authoritative historical record of variant configurations, supporting compliance requirements and enabling sellers and administrators to review the complete evolution of product variants over time.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: The parent product snapshot this variant snapshot belongs to. Links to {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: The source variant whose state is captured in this snapshot. Links to {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: The SKU code of the variant at the time of snapshot creation. Unique identifier for inventory tracking.

plainFields.name: price_override
plainFields.description: The variant's price override at the time of snapshot. Null if the variant uses the product's base price. When present, this price takes precedence over the product's base_price.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant snapshot was created. Marks the point-in-time when the variant state was captured.

models.description:
Inventory history records tracking stock level changes per product variant.

Each record represents a single stock movement with quantity change (positive for restocks/refunds, negative for orders/adjustments), reason for the change, and timestamp. Current stock for any variant is calculated by summing all quantity_change values for that variant.

This is an append-only audit trail used for inventory tracking and dispute resolution. Stock is never stored directly; it's always computed from the sum of all history records.

**Change Types:**
- Positive: Restock, Cancellation refund, Refund return
- Negative: Order placement, Inventory adjustment/loss

**Related Entities:**
- {@link shopping_mall_product_variants} - The variant whose stock is being tracked

foreignFields.description: Reference to the product variant whose inventory is being tracked. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id

models.name: shopping_mall_product_inventory_histories

plainFields.description: Quantity change in stock. Positive values indicate stock additions (restock, cancellation refund, refund return). Negative values indicate stock deductions (order placement, inventory adjustment/loss). Current stock equals the sum of all history records for a variant.
plainFields.name: quantity_change

plainFields.description: Reason for the inventory change. Examples: 'restock', 'order', 'adjustment', 'cancellation', 'refund', 'loss'. Provides audit trail context for each stock movement.
plainFields.name: reason

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the inventory change occurred. Used for chronological ordering of stock movements and audit trail purposes.
plainFields.name: created_at

models.description:
Normalized key-value pairs for product variant options, enabling 1NF compliance by decomposing complex option attributes into atomic units.

Each record represents a single attribute of a product variant (e.g., color="Red", size="Large"). This decomposition replaces JSON storage in the parent variant table, enabling proper querying and filtering by option type and value.

**Key Features:**
- One record per option attribute per variant
- Unique constraint ensures each variant has only one value per option key
- Supports arbitrary option types (color, size, material, etc.)
- Enables efficient filtering and searching by option values

**Relationships:**
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_product_variants} (many options per variant)
- Referenced when creating variant snapshots for order items

foreignFields.description: The product variant this option belongs to. Links the key-value pair to its parent variant for product configuration. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_options

plainFields.description: The option attribute name (e.g., "color", "size", "material", "pattern"). Defines the category of the variant option. Used as the key in the key-value pair structure.
plainFields.name: key

plainFields.description: The option attribute value (e.g., "Red", "Large", "Cotton", "Striped"). The actual value for the specified option key. Subject to full-text search for filtering products by option values.
plainFields.name: value

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant option was created. Automatically set upon record creation.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant option was last updated. Automatically updated when the option value changes.
plainFields.name: updated_at

models.description:
Junction table linking product snapshots to product images, capturing which images were attached to a product at the time of snapshot creation.

This table implements the snapshot principle requirement that product snapshots include all fields including images. When a product snapshot is created, all images attached to that product are linked through this junction table, preserving the complete visual state of the product at that moment.

Being a subsidiary entity, this table is managed through parent snapshot operations and does not require independent API endpoints. The immutable nature of snapshots means these image associations are never modified after creation.

foreignFields.description: The product snapshot to which this image belongs. References {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots.id}. Each snapshot can have multiple images attached.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id

foreignFields.description: The product image linked to this snapshot. References {@link shopping_mall_product_images.id}. Captures which specific images were attached to the product at snapshot creation time.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_image_id

models.name: shopping_mall_product_snapshot_images

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image was linked to the product snapshot during snapshot creation. Records the moment of association for audit purposes.
plainFields.name: created_at

models.description:
Normalized key-value pairs for variant snapshot option values, enabling 1NF-compliant storage of variant attributes at the point-in-time of snapshot creation.

Each record represents a single atomic attribute of a product variant (e.g., color='Red', size='Large') captured in a variant snapshot. This decomposition replaces storing option_values as JSON or serialized strings, enabling proper querying by option type and value for historical analysis and inventory reporting.

This table is essential for the snapshot principle, ensuring that variant option configurations at the time of purchase or modification are preserved immutably for dispute resolution, order fulfillment verification, and audit trail purposes.

Relationship: Multiple option values belong to a single {@link shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots} record, representing the complete option configuration of that variant at the snapshot moment.

foreignFields.description: The variant snapshot to which this option value belongs. Each snapshot can have multiple option values representing the complete variant configuration. {@link shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots.id}
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshot_id

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshot_option_values

plainFields.description: The type or category of the option attribute (e.g., 'color', 'size', 'material', 'style'). Stored in lowercase for consistent querying. Used for grouping and filtering variant options by category.
plainFields.name: option_key

models.name: shopping_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Customer shopping cart items storing specific product variants with quantities for purchase preparation.

Each cart item represents a single product variant (SKU) that a customer intends to purchase. The unit_price field captures the variant's price at the time of addition, enabling price change detection during checkout to alert customers if prices have changed.

Business constraints enforced at service layer:
- Maximum 99 units per cart item
- Maximum 50 distinct variants per customer cart
- Automatic combination of duplicate variant additions (sum quantities)

Cart items are transient and removed upon successful order placement. When variants are deleted or become out of stock, cart items are marked as unavailable but preserved for customer visibility.

References {@link shopping_mall_customers} for cart ownership and {@link shopping_mall_product_variants} for the specific SKU being purchased.

foreignFields.name: shopping_customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who owns this cart item. References {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: The specific product variant (SKU) in the cart. References {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units of this variant in the cart. Maximum allowed is 99 units per item. When the same variant is added multiple times, quantities are combined into a single cart item.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Price per unit at the time the item was added to cart. Used to detect price changes during checkout - if the current variant price differs from this stored value, the customer is notified of the price change. Stored as decimal for monetary precision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cart item was first added. Used for cart item ordering and pagination.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cart item was last modified (quantity change, etc.).

foreignFields.description: Customer who placed this order. References {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id

plainFields.name: total_price

plainFields.description: Derived order status computed from constituent order item statuses. Values: 'paid' (all items paid), 'shipped' (any item shipped), 'delivered' (all items delivered), 'cancelled' (all items cancelled), 'refunded' (all items refunded), 'partially_completed' (mixed statuses).
plainFields.name: status

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was created after successful payment.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was last updated, such as when order item statuses changed.
plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: shopping_mall_order_addresses
models.description:
Immutable shipping address snapshots captured at order placement time for legal compliance and audit trail purposes.

Each address record preserves the complete shipping information exactly as it was when the customer placed the order, ensuring that historical orders maintain accurate delivery records even if customers modify or delete addresses from their address book.

Contains recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, and country. Records are append-only and never modified after creation to maintain data integrity for dispute resolution and legal compliance.

References {@link shopping_mall_orders} via unique foreign key, establishing a one-to-one relationship where each order has exactly one shipping address snapshot.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order this shipping address belongs to. Each order has exactly one shipping address snapshot. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}

plainFields.name: recipient_name
plainFields.description: Full name of the person designated to receive the shipment at the delivery address.

plainFields.name: phone
plainFields.description: Contact phone number for the recipient, used for delivery coordination and shipping notifications.

plainFields.name: street
plainFields.description: Street address including house/apartment number for the delivery location.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City or locality name for the delivery address.

plainFields.name: state
plainFields.description: State, province, or administrative region for the delivery address.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal or ZIP code for the delivery address.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country name or ISO country code for the delivery address.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipping address snapshot was created at order placement. Immutable - no updated_at field as records are never modified.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_items
models.description: Individual order items representing specific product variants purchased by customers. Each item maintains independent status tracking (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) enabling item-level cancellation/refund and multi-seller order handling. Contains complete snapshot data for product, variant, and seller at time of purchase for historical accuracy and dispute resolution. References the parent {@link shopping_mall_orders} and the selling {@link shopping_mall_sellers}. Product and variant references may become null if source entities are deleted, but snapshot data is preserved for order history integrity.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: The original variant at time of purchase. May be null if variant is deleted. References {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: product_description

plainFields.name: product_category_name
plainFields.description: Product category name at time of purchase. Snapshot value for order history display.

plainFields.name: product_base_price
plainFields.description: Product base price at time of purchase. Snapshot value preserved for price dispute resolution.

plainFields.description: Number of units purchased for this variant. Multiple quantities of the same variant are combined into a single order item.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Price per unit at time of purchase. Derived from variant price or product base price. Total for this item = quantity * unit_price.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of this order item. Valid values: 'paid' (awaiting shipment), 'shipped' (in transit), 'delivered' (received by customer), 'cancelled' (cancelled before shipping), 'refunded' (refunded after delivery). Each item has independent status enabling item-level operations.

plainFields.name: created_at

models.description:
Normalized key-value pairs capturing variant option values for order items at the point of purchase.

Each record stores a single option attribute (e.g., key='color', value='red') as an atomic unit, enabling proper 1NF compliance by avoiding JSON or serialized string storage in the parent order item table. This decomposition allows efficient querying by option type and value, and preserves the exact variant configuration that the customer purchased.

Created automatically when an order is placed, copying the option values from the selected product variant. Part of the snapshot principle implementation ensuring complete audit trails for dispute resolution.

References {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id} as the parent entity.

foreignFields.description: The order item for which this variant option was captured. References {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

models.description:
Junction table linking order shipments to order items, enabling sellers to bundle multiple items from the same seller into a single shipment with one tracking number.

This table implements the many-to-one relationship between shipments and order items, where:
- A shipment can contain multiple order items (same seller bundling)
- An order item can belong to exactly one shipment (unique constraint)

When a seller creates a shipment and selects order items to ship, records are created in this junction table. The shipment's carrier name and tracking number apply to all bundled items.

Relationships:
- References {@link shopping_mall_order_shipments} for the shipment record
- References {@link shopping_mall_order_items} for the individual order items

The unique constraint on order_item_id ensures each order item is shipped exactly once, preventing duplicate shipment assignments.

foreignFields.description: Reference to the shipment that contains this order item. Links to {@link shopping_mall_order_shipments.id} to associate the order item with carrier and tracking information.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_shipment_id

foreignFields.description: Reference to the order item being shipped. Links to {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}. Unique constraint ensures each order item can only be assigned to one shipment.
foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id

models.name: shopping_mall_order_shipment_items

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: shopping_mall_order_shipment_audit_logs
models.description: Immutable audit trail for shipment lifecycle events capturing creation, status transitions, delivery confirmations (both manual by customer and automatic after 14 days), and administrative interventions. Each log entry records the event type, previous and new status, responsible actor (seller, customer, admin, or system), connection context (IP, URL), and timestamp. Provides complete traceability for dispute resolution and compliance. References {@link shopping_mall_order_shipments} for shipment association.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the shipment being audited. {@link shopping_mall_order_shipments.id}.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Type of shipment lifecycle event. Values: 'created' (shipment created by seller), 'status_changed' (manual status update), 'delivered_manually' (customer confirmed delivery), 'delivered_auto' (automatic delivery after 14 days), 'admin_override' (administrator intervention).

plainFields.name: old_status
plainFields.description: Previous shipment status before the event. Null for 'created' events which have no prior state. Values: 'preparing', 'shipped', 'delivered'.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: New shipment status after the event. Values: 'preparing' (initial), 'shipped' (carrier has package), 'delivered' (received by customer).

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who performed the action. Values: 'seller' (merchant shipping items), 'customer' (buyer confirming delivery), 'admin' (administrator override), 'system' (automatic process for 14-day delivery).

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: UUID of the actor who performed the action. References shopping_mall_sellers.id, shopping_mall_customers.id, or shopping_mall_admins.id based on actor_type. Null for 'system' actor type.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client that triggered the event. Used for security audit and fraud detection. Null for system-triggered events.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL path of the API endpoint that triggered the event. Provides context for understanding which operation caused the status change. Null for system-triggered events.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional additional context or reason for the event. Used for admin override explanations, automatic delivery confirmation details, or other relevant information.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit log entry was created. Represents the exact moment the shipment event occurred. Used for chronological ordering and time-based analysis.

models.description:
Customer-initiated cancellation requests for order items with 'paid' status.

Customers can request cancellation for order items that have not yet been shipped (status: paid). Each request captures the customer's reason, tracks the approval workflow through pending/approved/rejected statuses, and records seller responses including rejection reasons when applicable.

Key relationships:
- References {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id} for the item being cancelled (1:1 - one request per item)
- References {@link shopping_mall_customers.id} for the requesting customer
- Seller context is derived through the order item's seller association

Business rules:
- Only order items with 'paid' status can have cancellation requests
- Approved cancellations trigger automatic refund and stock restoration
- All state changes are captured in {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots} for audit

foreignFields.description: The order item being cancelled. References {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}. Only one cancellation request allowed per order item.

plainFields.name: seller_response

models.description:
Immutable snapshots preserving complete state of cancellation requests at each stage of their lifecycle. Created automatically when a cancellation request is submitted and when a seller responds (approve/reject). Records the transition from previous status to new status, along with the customer's reason for cancellation, seller's response, and rejection reason if applicable. Provides complete audit trail for dispute resolution and legal compliance as required by the snapshot principle. Each snapshot represents a single state transition and cannot be modified or deleted.

Related to {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests} for the parent cancellation request entity.

foreignFields.description: The cancellation request this snapshot captures. {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id}

plainFields.name: new_status

models.description:
Customer reviews and ratings for purchased products, containing rating (1-5 stars), optional text content, and references to customer, product, and order for purchase verification.

Supports soft delete to preserve reviews when customers delete accounts, displaying as 'deleted user' while maintaining review content for product rating calculations. Enforces one review per product per order constraint to prevent duplicate reviews.

Reviews can only be written for delivered order items. When customers edit their reviews, snapshots are created separately in {@link shopping_mall_review_snapshots} for audit trails and dispute resolution.

models.description:
Immutable snapshot records of review edits preserving previous and new rating values and text content. Created automatically when customers modify their reviews to maintain complete edit history for dispute resolution and audit purposes.

Each snapshot captures the state transition from previous to new values, recording when the change occurred and what values changed. Snapshots are never deleted even if the parent review is soft-deleted, ensuring permanent audit trails for the snapshot principle.

Supports the platform's financial accountability model where customer feedback disputes may require historical evidence of what was originally written versus current state.
